pages.title: The Poison Bottle
pages.subtitle: Examination photographs and the preview record

blocks.heading: Before the Death
blocks.text: The real glass bottle stood on an open stand at the 6:20–6:28 PM preview. There was no glass cover. It had arrived closed.

blocks.heading: The Bottle’s Seal
blocks.text: New red paper with a silver backing crossed the stopper. A split at the back was hidden from the front.

blocks.heading: Paper Found in Grant’s Glass
blocks.text: The scrap resembles the unused sealing paper: red on one side, silver on the other. Their torn edges do not make a unique match.

pages.title: The Toast and the Camera
pages.subtitle: Service records, photographs and the technician’s report

blocks.heading: Grant’s Individual Drink
blocks.text: The paid toast order included flavoring for Grant’s glass. The shared punch was unflavored.

blocks.heading: The Same Crest-Engraved Glass
blocks.text: The shop delivered Grant’s crest-engraved glass before setup. It stood unwrapped and uncovered. He drank from it; the water bottle stayed sealed.

blocks.heading: The Room Camera
blocks.text: The request was to remove the room from the public monitor. The approved work disconnected its power. The network cable stayed attached; the unpowered camera recorded nothing.
A technology demonstrator supplied sample images and proposed connecting to this existing camera.

pages.title: Record Comparisons
pages.subtitle: Original records and the versions circulated afterward

blocks.heading: Purchase and Loan
blocks.text: Original contents were required, not an empty bottle or replica. The seller retained them; no cancellation or substitution arrived. Museum staff had the dealer’s note and full terms before the gala. Loan description: harmless (“inert”).

blocks.heading: Staff and Press
blocks.text: October 29: Dr. Art E. Fact sought clarification before opening. Reply: “Unresolved. Keep closed.” Staff got the full query, seller’s note and warning. Reed DeLabel’s press copy kept “inert” and deleted: “Purchase condition requires original contents to remain.”
blocks.strike: Purchase condition requires original contents to remain.

blocks.heading: Seal Dates
blocks.text: Signed treatment: October 30, 2026. Chip’s insurance copy: October 29, 2026. Same red paper across the stopper.

blocks.heading: Access Checks
blocks.text: After the preview, staff keys and the founder’s spare could both open the storage cupboard. Tour record: alcove closed, hanging load removed; the group returned to public cases, never entering Grant’s room or approaching his place.

blocks.heading: Paige Interview
blocks.text: Service left Grant’s glass and returned to the kitchen about the added course. Grant challenged Paige for following him into his private room. Their agreed gift interview was being recorded. Grant would discuss tonight’s gift announcement or speak tomorrow.

blocks.heading: Robin Interview
blocks.text: Robin handed over the demand: return the bowl intact or hold a hearing. The museum already had a copy. Grant refused it while answering the reporter in his private room, not the public podium.

blocks.heading: Film and Podcast
blocks.text: Before the gala, production received picture and sound together: “Jacket take,” chair scrape, falling empty jacket, clatter, empty chair. The uncut podcast keeps this sequence; its teaser starts after the spoken cue.

blocks.heading: Photo Files
blocks.text: After the preview, the editor copied the whole camera card before returning it: real bottle on open stand, no toast photo. The photographer later made the news-agency version.

blocks.heading: Gift
blocks.text: The director required board approval, even if the gift was lost. Lawyer stopped the acceptance announcement; toast stayed booked. Unsigned original withdrawn at the announcement desk. Coordinator and Grant held separate public and private copies.

blocks.heading: Family and Claim
blocks.text: The family successor’s board seat required gift acceptance. Appointment was requested while Grant lived. The letter names claimants; it is not a ministry return order. Ownership objection accompanies earlier acquisition advice.

blocks.heading: Bowl Policies
blocks.text: The bowl label no longer claims settled ownership; it warns of missing papers. The museum withdrew its old lender-description shortcut and now requires supporting review. The clipping corrects an owner’s name. It never says poison was neutralized.

blocks.heading: Gallery Plans
blocks.text: Grant rejected live and screen versions. Both styling plans crossed out the cover over his place. Bottle stand: no glass front. Textile slides: enlarged stitches only.

blocks.heading: Sale and Painting
blocks.text: Bowl withdrawn from sale; bottle on loan. Permission to reproduce Vincent’s painting withheld; final payment at risk. Endorsement withdrawn before public announcement.

blocks.heading: Materials and Value
blocks.text: Sculpture: resin mixed with metal powder; corrected label, reduced final payment. Sample: bronze powder and gold leaf, not red-and-silver paper. Family appraisal used a damaged comparison for an intact piece.

blocks.heading: Payments
blocks.text: Elon billed before installation; accounts rejected his invoice. Wages used restricted funds without approval. Fabric used another client’s commission advance. School places used workshop funds; paid weekend session canceled.

blocks.heading: Publicity Photo
blocks.text: Earlier photo: public gallery and podium, not Grant’s room. Crop hides the disputed purchase; a commercial image was supplied as news photography.
The artist supplied a painting. The wooden model has visible joints; the preview bottle is glass. No model swap was authorized.

blocks.heading: The Damaged Frame
blocks.text: The first report called the crack old damage. The handler’s signed correction records damage during delivery.
